title: Concordance of the modified wells score with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism in an imaging-selected cohort: A retrospective single-center study

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Concordance of the modified wells score with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism in an imaging-selected cohort: A retrospective single-center study》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · abstract-1-1】Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a major diagnostic challenge in emergency medicine. Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the gold standard but is frequently overused. The modified Wells Score (mWS) estimates pre-test probability and may reduce inappropriate imaging at triage. We evaluated the concordance between mWS and CTPA-confirmed PE in a tertiary emergency department.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Concordance of the modified wells score with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism in an imaging-selected cohort: A retrospective single-center study》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We retrospectively analyzed all patients undergoing CTPA for suspected PE over 24 months. As all patients had already undergone CTPA, this design reflects concordance within an imaging-selected cohort, not triage performance. mWS values were assigned by consensus between two readers, blinded to CTPA results; D-dimer was not incorporated. AUC was computed from the full ordinal mWS range; sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV were calculated at the conventional mWS ≥ 4 threshold. Spearman's correlation assessed the mWS-PE severity association.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Among 691 patients, 103 (14.9%) had CTPA-confirmed PE. At mWS ≥ 4, sensitivity was 86.4%, specificity 98.6%, AUC 0.943 (95% CI: 0.91-0.97). The Youden index identified mWS ≥ 3 as optimal (sensitivity 89.3%, specificity 95.7%); ≥ 4 was retained for analysis. Under this threshold, 594 patients (86.0%) fell below the cut-off, suggesting avoidable imaging, though unconfirmed in non-imaged patients. Fourteen false-negative (3 central PE) and eight false-positive cases were identified. Higher mWS correlated moderately with PE burden (ρ = 0.578, p < 0.01).

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Concordance of the modified wells score with CTPA-confirmed pulmonary embolism in an imaging-selected cohort: A retrospective single-center study》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】Among 691 patients, 103 (14.9%) had CTPA-confirmed PE. At mWS ≥ 4, sensitivity was 86.4%, specificity 98.6%, AUC 0.943 (95% CI: 0.91-0.97). The Youden index identified mWS ≥ 3 as optimal (sensitivity 89.3%, specificity 95.7%); ≥ 4 was retained for analysis. Under this threshold, 594 patients (86.0%) fell below the cut-off, suggesting avoidable imaging, though unconfirmed in non-imaged patients. Fourteen false-negative (3 central PE) and eight false-positive cases were identified. Higher mWS correlated moderately with PE burden (ρ = 0.578, p < 0.01).

【Conclusion · abstract-4-1】mWS showed strong concordance with CTPA-confirmed PE; diagnostic accuracy exceeding pooled meta-analytic estimates likely reflects consensus-scoring methodology rather than genuine superiority. Prospective, multicentre validation incorporating D-dimer testing and independent scoring is warranted before routine implementation.
